newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian base metals market closed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: Indian base metals market closed for holiday.

text.p: The Bombay metals market was closed on Thursday for a national holiday. Trading resumes on Friday.
On Wednesday, copper fell slightly in line with the metal's price movements on the London Metals Exchange (LME). Other base metals were steady in dull trade.
"Copper is weak on LME though it is expected recover," said Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
Copper lost 25 rupees to 13,650 rupees per quintal. It was steady on Tuesday at 13,675 rupees per quintal.

Tin was steady at 31,500 rupees per quintal and so was nickel at 36,500 rupees per quintal. Aluminium was unchanged at 7,450 rupees per quintal. Zinc was quiet at 7,900 rupees per quintal. Lead was offered at 4,550 rupees per quintal.
